task: Build KPI success 1's id boost for DAEO-zqvn (W2-13). When a question holds an id among other words, the chunks that hold that id verbatim as a whole token come first in `ranked`, marked `exact`; `hits` does not change.
status: DONE. Committed `febe5f6403d5`; all four suites I was asked to run are green.
work_completed: Step 0 first. (a) The write to `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/.sandbox-trial-DAEO-zqvn` failed as it should (`OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system`). (b) `git hash-object -w --stdin` worked (it printed a blob id) and `git update-index --refresh` worked (exit 0). `GOV_ROLE=engineer`, `GOV_TICKET=DAEO-zqvn`, top level `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-13`, branch `w2/W2-13`. `python3 -c "import gov; print(gov.__file__)"` printed `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-13/src/gov/__init__.py`. Then I built the boost in `lexical._ranked`. The first FTS5 query is now the question as a phrase OR each id the question holds (other than the question itself, at most `MAX_TERMS`) as a phrase, still in that query's BM25 order. A returned chunk is `exact: true` if one of its lines holds the whole question string (as before) or if its text holds one of those ids verbatim, case and all, as a whole token. `hits` is still built only from the chunks that hold the whole question. The word query and `TOP_K` are unchanged, and exact chunks are left out of the word list, so each chunk appears once. I added a public `lexical.whole_id(name)`, the same regex `gov retrieve`'s stated gap already used inline, and `command.py` now calls it instead of its own copy: behaviour is identical and the unused `import re` is gone. The rule is written into the module docstring's description of `ranked`.
files_changed: src/gov/retrieval/lexical.py (+23 −6); src/gov/retrieve/command.py (+1 −2); tests/unit/retrieval/test_w2_13_id_boost.py (new, +111). Total +135 −8.
evidence: Commit `febe5f6403d5` on `w2/W2-13`, parent `962fc43467f7`. Trailers: Task: DAEO-zqvn / Role: engineer / Implements: DEC-725 / Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Before committing, `/home/usain/Dynamic-Agentic-Engineering-OS/.git/hooks` held only `*.sample` files. After the commit, `git log --oneline -2` shows `febe5f6403d5`, then `962fc43467f7`; `git status --short` shows none of my paths, only untracked files that are not mine (see discoveries).
tests: tests/unit/retrieval: 116 passed, 1 skipped (`test_lexical.py:54`, no `govbridge` module; it was skipped before my change too). tests/unit/retrieve: 15 passed. tests/acceptance/W1-17: 65 passed. tests/acceptance/W2-87: 21 passed. The new builder test has five cases, all passing. (1) Holder against noise: for `QX-4471 gauge reading`, the noise files mention `QX`, `4471`, `qx-4471`, `QX-44710`, `QX-4471-b` and the other words more often; the holder ranks first, it is the only exact chunk, and `hits == []`. (2) `QX-4471` asked alone still ranks the holder first. (3) A chunk holding the whole question (`QX-9 dial reading`) stays boosted, beside the chunk that holds only `QX-9`, and `hits` is just that one line. (4) A question with no id gets no boost. (5) The boost costs at most two MATCH statements per question. Every case checks that every exact chunk ranks above every non-exact one and that each chunk appears once. I did not read or run tests/acceptance/W2-13.
discoveries: (1) The brief gives the head as `962fc434c1f5`, but the real head is `962fc43467f7`. The first 8 digits match, the commit subject matches, and the brief's other two hashes (`c38a5b49bc86`, `15e235d637bc`) resolved and are consistent with it, so this looks like a typo; I went ahead. (2) Since my session started, untracked files have appeared at the worktree root: `.bash_profile`, `.bashrc`, `.gitconfig`, `.gitmodules`, `.idea`, `.mcp.json`, `.profile`, `.ripgreprc`, `.vscode`, `.zprofile`, `.zshrc`. They are probably sandbox placeholders; they are not mine, I did not touch them and I did not commit them. `pytest-of-usain/` was already there when I started.
risks: (1) For a question with words plus a common id (e.g. `DEC-725 ...`), the first query now pulls every chunk whose tokens match the id phrase, text included. That is the same work `gov retrieve "DEC-725"` already does, so it adds no query, but its cost grows with how often the id occurs. I measured no p95: this worktree's store was built with the base code and reads as stale, and I may not rebuild it. (2) Chunks that match the id phrase but not verbatim (e.g. lowercase `qx-4471`) get no boost and come back through the word query, as intended.
lessons: The boost lives in the same FTS5 query as the exact route, so the count per question stays at two MATCH statements at most and `test_w2_13_rerank_work.py`'s bound did not need to change. The whole-token rule is now one function, `lexical.whole_id`, used by the boost and by the stated gap.
